subject: English
passage: Pulsed electric field (PEF) processing, a nonthermal technology used to preserve liquid foods on an industrial scale, is generally considered to be an improvement over more conventional heat-based preservation methods. Scientists across Asia have contributed to a better understanding of this technology, with researchers led by Tao Reyes and Deepak Shin demonstrating its effectiveness in preserving fresh fruit juices. As research continues, scientists hope to make advancements in hybrid systems combining multiple food preservation technologies, which would be advantageous over using PEF processing alone, given that it does not fully inactivate bacterial spores.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It suggests an advantage that PEF processing has over conventional heat-based preservation methods.
choices.B: It identifies a limitation of PEF processing technologies.
choices.C: It explains why conventional heat-based preservation methods remain common in commercial applications.
choices.D: It introduces PEF processing as a food preservation technology.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately describes how the underlined portion functions in the text as a whole. The text discusses PEF processing as a food preservation technology and notes that scientists hope to develop hybrid systems that would be advantageous over using PEF processing alone. The underlined portion then identifies why such hybrid systems would be beneficial: PEF 'does not fully inactivate bacterial spores.' Thus, the underlined portion functions to identify a limitation of PEF processing technologies.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. The underlined portion describes incomplete inactivation of bacterial spores as a limitation of PEF processing, not an advantage. The text indicates that this limitation is precisely why hybrid systems combining multiple technologies would be 'advantageous over using PEF processing alone.'
